title: Personal Agent Comparison Criteria Matcher
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: AI for EE Research
description: Classification activity in which learners place each of eight questions a researcher might ask about a personal, always-on AI agent under one of eight comparison criteria: Where it runs, Blast radius, Approval model, Usage metering, Data exposure, Memory, Claim verification, and Activity audit. The criteria buttons are shuffled once per learner. Each submitted answer gets one attempt and immediate feedback with the correct criterion and a one-sentence reason, and the run ends with a score out of 8, a mastery statement at 7 of 8, and a one-line test per criterion that the learner could run on a real product.

educational.topic: Criteria for comparing personal and always-on AI agents
learningObjectives: Classify each of eight questions about a personal agent under the comparison criterion it addresses, with at least 7 of 8 correct
Explain what a question about an agent is really asking, using criteria that transfer to products that do not exist yet
prerequisites: Agent blast radius, usage metering, agent data exposure, vendor claim verification, and overnight activity audit
Cloud agent computer, self-hosted agent, and the approval model

canvasDimensions.controlHeight: responsive (128 to 204 by width; 50 on the end screen)

accessibility.notes: describe() provides a screen-reader description; all controls are native HTML buttons reachable with the Tab key and activated with Enter or Space; focus moves to Next after Submit; chosen, correct and incorrect states use a symbol (filled circle, check mark, X) and border style as well as a blue/orange color-blind-safe palette; all text is 16 px or larger.

controls.label: Where it runs, Blast radius, Approval model, Usage metering, Data exposure, Memory, Claim verification, Activity audit
controls.purpose: Eight criterion buttons in an order shuffled once per learner. Pressing one selects that criterion for the current question; the choice can be changed until Submit. Disabled after submission, when the correct criterion is marked with a check mark and a wrong pick with an X.

controls.label: Submit
controls.purpose: Commits the selected criterion as the single attempt for the current question. Enabled only when a criterion is selected and the question has not been submitted.

controls.label: Next Question / See Score
controls.purpose: Enabled after submission. Advances to the next question in the fixed order, and after question 8 shows the score screen.

controls.label: More Tests
controls.purpose: Shown only on the score screen when the eight one-line tests do not fit on one page; pages through them.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Eight-way classification with one attempt per item, explanatory feedback, and per-learner shuffling of the answer options
keyQuestions: Which criterion does this question test?
Is this question about where the agent runs or about what it can reach?
Does a vendor's statement count as verification?
commonMisconceptions: A comparison is about features and price only
A vendor's statement about safety is itself the verification
Where an agent runs is the same as what it can reach
assessmentOpportunities: A first-attempt score of at least 7 of 8 matching the answer key is evidence of mastery
Reading the list of criteria is exploration and is not evidence
Learner runs one-line tests from the end screen against a real product with a throwaway account
